boundary: Local read-only audit of the closed compiler proposal, selected whole cuts and consequential cited source passages. The independent native reviewer remained running in the observed snapshot. This report is neither registry admission nor a whole-graph precision assessment.
mechanical_check_limit: Exact quote containment and canonical-hash matches establish quotation and object binding, not semantic entailment. The 206 evidence objects contain repeated quotations; they are not 206 independent validations.
overall_scope_judgment: No new whole-mechanism conflation was identified in the six proposed definitions. The two multi-method definitions explicitly use shared_purpose and null common mechanisms with explanatory unknown-reason fields; null here denotes the comparison level, not ignorance of the per-use chemistry. Membership is restricted to the selected cuts and retained contextual qualifications. One known unsupported parent assertion remains in the immutable ATAC occurrence.

findings.judgment: DBiT/DR/Drop/SPLiT share transcript-to-DNA/origin-preservation purpose; scBS/SLAM share chemical-state-to-sequence-library purpose. Neither group establishes interchangeable chemistry, equal complete cuts, identical readout interpretation, or equal performance. Four other definitions each have only one supplied occurrence; shared_mechanism is a schema relation label, not evidence of four cross-method shared mechanisms.

The selected unit ends with three-round-barcoded cells/nuclei physically allocated into sublibraries. The fourth PCR index is not yet installed. It supports construction of origin-bearing intermediates, not a complete four-barcode identity or a guaranteed unique single-cell address. The proposal explicitly excludes fourth-index/PCR/library completion and retains collision risk. Any later display must retain this qualification.

source_evidence.quote: After this step, cells from all wells are pooled and redistributed into a new 96-well plate, where an in-cell ligation reaction appends a second well-specific barcode to the cDNA. The third-round barcode, which also contains a unique molecular identifier (UMI), is then appended with another round of pooling, splitting, and ligation. After three rounds of barcoding, the cells are pooled, split into sublibraries, and sequencing barcodes are introduced by PCR. This final step provides a fourth barcode, while also making it possible to sequence different numbers of cells in each sublibrary.
source_evidence.rationale: Two pool/split ligations precede physical sublibrary partition and later fourth PCR index.

source_evidence.quote: After sequencing, each transcriptome is assembled by combining reads containing the same four-barcode combination (Fig. 1A [link: #F1], Fig. S1A [link: #SD1]).
source_evidence.rationale: Downstream four-barcode grouping explains use of partial origin-encoded intermediates.

source_evidence.quote: After the third round of barcoding, 70 μL of 10% Triton-X100 is added to the cell solution before spinning it down for 5 min at 1000G and 4˚C. We carefully aspirated the supernatant, leaving about 30 μL to avoid removing the pellet. We then resuspended the cells in 4 mL of wash buffer (4 mL of 1X PBS, 40 μL of 10% Triton X-100 and 10 μL of SUPERase In RNase Inhibitor) and spun down for 5 min at 1000G at 4˚C. We then aspirated the supernatant and resuspended in 50 μL of PBS-RI. After counting cells, we aliquoted them into sublibraries (in 1.7 mL tubes).
source_evidence.rationale: Wash/count/physical allocation define the selected output; later lysis is outside the cut.

findings.judgment: Ad-1x installs cell-specific identity in transcript-derived cDNA; most joint amplicons carry Ad-2 at both ends. Genome-origin association also depends on separately handled single-cell samples and allocation of their mixed amplification products. Do not infer that every gDNA/cDNA amplicon contains the molecular cell barcode, that genome/transcript halves are pure analyte classes, or that Ad-2 random priming is a random-sequence UMI. The proposal preserves these distinctions and uses cited MALBAC only as contextual looping evidence, retaining DR seven-round handling.

source_evidence.quote: First, hand-picked single cells are lysed and reverse transcribed using a poly-A primer (called Adapter-1x or Ad-1x) including cell-specific barcodes, a 5′ Illumina adapter and a T7 promoter overhang to convert mRNA to single stranded cDNA (ss cDNA)
source_evidence.rationale: Single-cell poly(A) RT installs cell-specific Ad-1x, adapter and T7 promoter.

source_evidence.quote: The gDNA and single stranded cDNA are then subjected to quasilinear whole genome amplification, as previously described, using an adapter with a defined 27 nucleotide sequence at the 5′ end followed by 8 random nucleotides (Ad-2)^(7) (Fig. 1a). After 7 rounds of amplification, the gDNA and cDNA are copied to generate a variety of different short amplicon (0.5–2.5 kb) species, with a majority of amplicons containing adapter Ad-2 at both ends and a small fraction of cDNA derived amplicons containing Ad-2 at one end and Ad-1x at the other (Fig. 1a).
source_evidence.rationale: Joint quasilinear amplification retains genomic and transcript-derived material and adapter diversity.

source_evidence.quote: After 7 sounds of quasilinear amplification, samples were split in two. One half of the sample was processed for gDNA sequencing, the other half was processed for mRNA sequencing.
source_evidence.rationale: The joint product is split into two physical halves for genome/transcript branches.

source_evidence.quote: The masked genomes mm10 and hg19 were created by replacing all the coding sequences within the genome with “N”. This is because the fraction used to sequence gDNA contains sequences that could originate from the cDNA within coding regions (Fig 1a and Supplementary Fig. 13). By masking the coding sequences within the genome, such ambiguous reads that might arise from either gDNA or cDNA are discarded computationally leaving only reads that arise from gDNA.
source_evidence.rationale: Downstream coding masks document genomic/cDNA ambiguity within the nominal genomic half.

findings.judgment: scBS bisulfite conversion/fragmentation occurs before adapter tagging, retaining a methylation-sensitive DNA sequence readout. SLAM IAA covalently modifies s4U in RNA and produces RT-dependent T>C information through Quant-seq. This is not literal RNA U-to-C replacement or physical enrichment of the labeled RNA fraction. Endogenous methylation versus metabolic-label meaning, priming/coverage, amplification, 3-prime sampling and downstream interpretation remain distinct. The definition explicitly conditions biological interpretation on substrate and chemistry, without promising perfect conversion or universal modification discrimination.

source_evidence.quote: For scBS-Seq we used a modification of Post-Bisulfite Adaptor Tagging (PBAT)^(7), where bisulfite treatment is performed first, resulting in simultaneous DNA fragmentation and conversion of unmethylated cytosines (Fig. 1a).
source_evidence.rationale: Bisulfite before adapters fragments DNA and converts unmethylated cytosines.

source_evidence.quote: Then, complementary strand synthesis is primed using custom oligos containing Illumina adapter sequences and a 3′ stretch of nine random nucleotides. This step is performed five times to ensure that maximum numbers of DNA strands are tagged and to generate multiple copies of each fragment. After capture of the tagged strands, the second adapter is similarly integrated, and PCR amplification is performed with indexed primers allowing multiple single-cell libraries to be sequenced together.
source_evidence.rationale: Repeated first tagging, capture, second tagging and indexed PCR complete construction.

source_evidence.quote: In SLAM-seq, we employed the primary thiol-reactive compound iodoacetamide (IAA), which covalently attaches a carboxyamidomethyl-group to s^(4)U by nucleophilic substitution (Fig.1a).
source_evidence.rationale: IAA covalently carboxyamidomethylates s4U by nucleophilic substitution.

source_evidence.quote: Here, we report thiol(SH)-linked alkylation for the metabolic sequencing of RNA (SLAM-seq), an orthogonal chemistry approach that uncovers s^(4)U at single-nucleotide-resolution by reverse-transcription-dependent thymine-to-cytosine-conversions in a high-throughput sequencing-compatible manner.
source_evidence.rationale: The state readout is RT-dependent T>C recoding.

source_evidence.quote: For a typical SLAM-seq experiment, 5 µg total RNA were treated with 10 mM iodoacetamide under optimal reaction conditions and subsequently ethanol precipitated and subjected to Quant-seq 3′ end mRNA library preparation.
source_evidence.rationale: Implemented RNA treatment, ethanol recovery and Quant-seq handoff.

source_evidence.quote: Quant-seq uses total RNA as input, hence no prior poly(A) enrichment or rRNA depletion is required. Library generation is initiated by oligo-dT-anchor priming. Primer already contains Illumina-compatible linker sequences (green).
source_evidence.rationale: Oligo-dT-anchor priming adds a linker without prior poly(A) enrichment.

source_evidence.quote: The library is then amplified, introducing the sequences required for cluster generation (shown in red and purple). External barcodes (BC) for multiplexing are introduced during the PCR amplification step.
source_evidence.rationale: PCR installs cluster-generation interfaces and bulk external indices.

parent_assertions: Do not return the analytical amplification product to the sequencing library.
analytical qPCR amplicons are not returned to this path.
findings.definition_wording: analytic amplicons are not asserted to rejoin sequencing material.
findings.judgment: The primary supports withdrawing an aliquot, running separate qPCR and using it to choose cycles for the remaining 45 microlitre reaction. It does not establish an experimental prohibition or categorical disposal fate for analytical amplicons. The compiler definition properly expresses lack of an asserted return, rather than a never-return rule, and retains the measurement-to-production controller. This wording does not repair, retract or newly validate the categorical imperative still embedded in the source occurrence and accepted parent. Keep that residual defect visible in downstream provenance and scientific caveats.

source_evidence.quote: To reduce GC and size bias in our PCR we monitored the PCR reaction using qPCR in order to stop amplification prior to saturation. To do this, we amplified the full libraries for 5 cycles, after 5 cycles we took an aliquot of the PCR reaction and added 10 μl of the PCR cocktail with Sybr Green at a final concentration of 0.6x. We ran this reaction for 20 cycles, to determine the additional number of cycles needed for the remaining 45 μL reaction.
source_evidence.rationale: A removed aliquot's qPCR determines additional production cycles.

source_evidence.quote: The libraries were purified using a Qiagen PCR cleanup kit yielding a final library concentration of ~30 nM in 20 μL. Libraries were amplified for a total of 10–12 cycles.
source_evidence.rationale: Production ends in PCR cleanup; cycle total and concentration are observations.

findings.judgment: DBiT A/B intersections encode spatial bins, not isolated cells; the selected multimodal tissue also contains ADT-derived DNA products. Drop first captures RNA noncovalently, destroys droplets, then makes covalent bead-associated cDNA during bulk RT. These outputs, tissue images and ancillary QC are not equivalent material states. Sparse loading and origin tags do not prove singlets or zero contamination. The proposal preserves these boundaries and does not invent a microscopy-to-flow feedback rule.

source_evidence.quote: Barcode A is composed of an oligo-dT sequence for binding mRNAs, a distinct spatial barcode Ai (i=1–50, 8mer), and a ligation linker (15mer). Reverse transcription was conducted during the first flow for in situ synthesis of first strand cDNAs that immediately incorporate barcode A.
source_evidence.rationale: Oligo-dT in situ RT writes a first spatial barcode.

source_evidence.quote: Also added to the barcode B reagents were T4 ligase and a complementary ligation linker to perform in situ ligation at the intersections, resulting in a mosaic of tissue pixels, each containing a distinct combination of barcodes Ai and Bj (i=1–50, j=1–50).
source_evidence.rationale: T4 ligase and complementary linker write intersecting spatial addresses.

source_evidence.quote: The oligo-dT region recognizes the poly-A tail of mRNAs and ADTs. DNA Barcode B consists of a ligation region, a barcode region, a UMI region and a PCR primer handle region. During the ligation process, the ligation region of barcode B is covalently linked to the ligation region of barcode A via a templated ligation step.
source_evidence.rationale: Both mRNA and polyadenylated ADT templates use the A/B interface.

source_evidence.quote: Immediately following droplet formation, the cell is lysed and releases its mRNAs, which then hybridize to the primers on the microparticle surface. The droplets are broken by adding a reagent to destabilize the oil-water interface (Experimental Procedures), and the microparticles collected and washed.
source_evidence.rationale: Lysis, hybridization and bead recovery precede covalent RT.

source_evidence.quote: The mRNAs are then reverse-transcribed in bulk, forming STAMPs, and template switching is used to introduce a PCR handle downstream of the synthesized cDNA (Zhu et al., 2001).
source_evidence.rationale: Bulk RT and template switching make cDNA STAMPs and a second PCR handle.

source_evidence.quote: To efficiently process thousands of STAMPs at once, we break droplets, collect the mRNA-bound microparticles, and reverse-transcribe the mRNAs (from the microparticle-attached primers) together in one reaction, forming covalent, stable STAMPs (Figure 2A, step 7, and Experimental Procedures).
source_evidence.rationale: The pooled RT makes stable covalent STAMPs.

source_evidence.quote: In Drop-Seq, across four conditions spanning 12.5 cells/µL to 100 cells/µL, the fraction of species-mixed STAMPs correlated with cell concentration (Figure 3A, 3B, S3B; Experimental Procedures), with cell doublet estimates ranging from 0.36% to 11.3% for the various cell concentrations tested (under the assumption that human-mouse doublets account for half of all doublets). This reflects the greater chance at higher cell concentrations that a droplet could encapsulate multiple cells.
source_evidence.rationale: Doublet risk changes with concentration; barcode identity does not guarantee a singlet.

source_evidence.quote: The largest source of single-cell impurity appeared to be ambient RNA that is present in the cell suspension (a first step of almost all single-cell methods) and presumably results from cells that are damaged during preparation
source_evidence.rationale: Ambient RNA limits attribution purity.

findings.judgment: 4sU enrichment retains RNA eluate after thiol biotinylation/capture/DTT release; scBS streptavidin retention and SLAM recoding are not that whole transformation. The wave estimator is a source-described computational chain, not numerical reproduction or a wet-lab mechanism. ATAC is an actual aliquot-measurement-cycle-choice controller, not any PCR/QC pair. ddRAD selection is physical automated agarose length-window recovery; adapter offset, empirical settings and pooling remain contextual, and selection alone does not certify unlike restriction ends. These four singleton cases cannot establish cross-method mechanism conservation or substitution.

source_evidence.quote: Biotinylated RNA was captured using Dynabeads MyOne Streptavidin T1 beads (Invitrogen). Biotinylated RNA was incubated with 100 μL Dynabeads with rotation for 15 min at 25°C. Beads were magnetically fixed and washed with 1× Dynabeads washing buffer.
source_evidence.rationale: Streptavidin binding, magnetic retention and washing.

source_evidence.quote: RNA-4sU was eluted with 100 μL of freshly prepared 100 mM dithiothreitol (DTT), and cleaned on RNeasy MinElute Spin columns (Qiagen).
source_evidence.rationale: DTT elution and column cleanup deliver recovered RNA.

source_evidence.quote: We next compared the 4 and 8 min normalized profiles to the 0 time point. For each of the 4 and 8 min samples, we chose the first bin downstream the TSS + 2.5 Kb (defined arbitrarily) where the sample’s signal is not higher than the 0 time point at the same position (up to 10%). This bin was defined as the ‘rough estimate’ of the boundary. If the first position (TSS + 2.5 Kb) was identified or no position was identified no boundary was determined.
source_evidence.rationale: Rough boundaries and explicit no-boundary outcomes are reference-relative.

source_evidence.quote: We looked for the local minimums of the derivative using the N.Yoder peak finder (mathworks.com) upstream the ‘rough estimate’ boundary; we considered only derivatives smaller than -0.01. We took the most downstream minimum relative to the ‘rough estimate’ boundary. Next, we identified the most downstream bin relative to the minimum (up to 2 Kb downstream to the ‘rough estimate’) where the derivative was close to 0 (> = -0.002) and defined it as the ‘refined estimate’. If no such bin was found we adhered to the ‘rough’ estimate.
source_evidence.rationale: Derivative minima, constrained returns toward zero and rough-boundary fallback define refinement.

source_evidence.quote: Next, the elongation rate was calculated by linearly fitting the averaged 4 and 8 min boundaries as a function of time. The slope of the linear fit was defined as the elongation rate. Next, the 50% confidence interval of the slope was defined as the confidence interval of the elongation rate. Only genes with confidence intervals better than 0.5 Kb/min were retained. The slope was also used to define the delay time, which was defined as being equal to the slope intersection with the time axis. The elongation rate was determined only for genes with delay times between -1 and 4 min.
source_evidence.rationale: Linear time fitting yields velocity, slope confidence and effective delay with filters.

source_evidence.quote: This calculation is based on the assumption that the elongation rate is uniform throughout the gene. However, it remains formally possible that the rate is slower at the beginning of the gene, in which case the calculated delay times may represent overestimates.
source_evidence.rationale: Uniform velocity is assumed; slower initial elongation can inflate effective delay.

source_evidence.quote: Note that when specifying target range for size selection, it is crucial to account for the additional 76bp of adapter DNA added in ligation.
source_evidence.rationale: Target coordinates include a 76-bp ligated-adapter contribution.

source_evidence.quote: Second, we tested the impact of changes in size-selection range and the efficacy of automated versus manual DNA size selection using automated size-selection technology, Pippin Prep (Sage Science, Beverly, MA; 2% agarose cartridge).
source_evidence.rationale: The automated selector uses an agarose cartridge, supporting gel-based fractionation.

promotion_and_reporting_limits: Native source review and final registry publication were not complete in the inspected compiler snapshot; do not report admitted definitions or shared components from this audit.
Ten decisions reference six proposed definitions: two multi-method purpose categories and four singleton mechanism prototypes. These are not six empirically shared components.

Whole-cut membership concerns the exact selected operations and interfaces, not an executable whole assay. Source-context/dependency gaps and incomplete downstream address/library layers remain use properties.
No substitution, interchangeable reagent route, performance equivalence, lineage/reuse, gold-standard factual completeness, or whole-graph scientific precision is established.
No SSH, native/model job, source alteration, parent repair, frozen-runtime change or Git source edit was performed for this audit.
